claims.body: On the penalty kill, Anaheim is near the top of the league, but the Islanders are one of the worst. Penalties should hurt the Islanders more than the Ducks. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mikael Granlund is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.

Mathew Barzal is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Victor Eklund has taken his spot beside Brayden Schenn and Calum Ritchie.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 37% last season.

NYI.head: Too close to call
NYI.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, while the Islanders will be without Barzal. Then again, the Islanders have home-ice advantage, and Anaheim will be without Terry. The Islanders can tip it if they get good looks.

ANA.head: A genuine toss-up
ANA.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, while the Islanders will be without Barzal. Then again, the Islanders have home-ice advantage, and Anaheim will be without Terry. The Ducks can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.
